performed_via_github_app.description:
Codecov provides highly integrated tools to group, merge, archive and compare coverage reports. Whether your team is comparing changes in a pull request or reviewing a single commit, Codecov will improve the code review workflow and quality.

## Code coverage done right.®

1. Upload coverage reports from your CI builds.
2. Codecov merges all builds and languages into one beautiful coherent report.
3. Get commit statuses, pull request comments and coverage overlay via our browser extension.

When Codecov merges your uploads it keeps track of the CI provider (inc. build details) and user specified context, e.g. `#unittest` ~ `#smoketest` or `#oldcode` ~ `#newcode`. You can track the `#unittest` coverage independently of other groups. [Learn more here](
http://docs.codecov.io/docs/flags)

Through **Codecov's Browser Extension** reports overlay directly in GitHub UI to assist in code review in [Chrome](https://chrome.google.com/webstore/detail/codecov/gedikamndpbemklijjkncpnolildpbgo) or Firefox (https://addons.mozilla.org/en-US/firefox/addon/codecov/)

*Highly detailed* **pull request comments** and *customizable* **commit statuses** will improve your team's workflow and code coverage incrementally.

**File backed configuration** all through the `codecov.yml`. 

## FAQ
- Do you **merge multiple uploads** to the same commit? **Yes**
- Do you **support multiple languages** in the same project? **Yes**
- Can you **group coverage reports** by project and/or test type? **Yes**
- How does **pricing** work? Only paid users can view reports and post statuses/comments.

body: Will this fix #2409? Worth looking at that example too

Heads-up on a possible collision: I've opened #2482, which **disables** two `Evaluator.Properties` QCheck properties rather than fixing them — including `Evaluator and stepper are consistent`, which this PR touches.

Motivation was narrow: case 7 ("Incremental eval agrees with fresh eval after a literal edit", #2457) reddened three unrelated CI runs in the last two days ([1](https://github.com/hazelgrove/hazel/actions/runs/33513972427), [2](https://github.com/hazelgrove/hazel/actions/runs/33513747011), [3](https://github.com/hazelgrove/hazel/actions/runs/33412342909)), and the confluence property failed on a random local seed while I was doing that. Since #2422 made the runner propagate a real exit status, both now block whatever PR they land on.

Explicitly not trying to pre-empt your fix — just to stop the bleeding until real fixes land. Two things worth knowing:

**1. This PR shouldn't be enough to re-enable the confluence property.** Your fix targets uncollapsed casts in indeterminate `if` branches (seed 773972249). The other known cause is binder freshening — `fun (x::x) -> x` reduces to `^^fold(fun (x::x) -> x)` under one engine and `^^fold(fun (x::x') -> x')` under the other (#2128, dup #2372), and `Equality.semantic.exp` doesn't equate the alpha-variants. #2482 pins that case as a deterministic expected-failure test, so it should still be red after this PR lands. If it isn't, your fix covered more than expected and the property can go straight back on.

**2. Both PRs edit `Test_Evaluator_Properties.re`, so expect a conflict.** #2482 restructures the confluence property fairly heavily: the both-engines run is extracted into a `reduce_both_engines` helper (`option((Exp.t, Exp.t))`, `None` for vacuous cases) that the property and the pin share, and the property body shrinks to a `switch` over it. If your regression test drives the engines directly it'll want to go through the same helper. Happy to defer — if you'd rather land this PR first, I can rebase #2482 on top of it, or drop the confluence half of #2482 entirely and keep only the #2457 disable, which is the one that actually caused the CI failures. Whichever you prefer.

Also flagging #2397 as unaddressed by either PR: "Pattern equivalence" exhausts node's 4 GB heap on ~1 seed in 6 and aborts the whole run, which shows up as a timeout rather than a test failure. Can't be pinned as an expected failure since an OOM kills the process — probably wants a lower `~count`/step limit.
